transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. AI. Um, well, I guess the main reason I'm here is that I just get pulled off track so incredibly easily. Like, I’ll be sitting down to finish this dashboard I’m supposed to be doing for my class... which, by the way, is a total nightmare because the software we use keeps crashing. I swear it hates my laptop. I was actually thinking of taking it to the Apple store to get checked, but the closest one is like an hour away by bus and the bus schedule around campus is just the worst right now because of all the construction on 4th street. 

But, um, what was I saying? Right, so I'll be trying to work, and then I get one Slack ping from a classmate, or I'll hear a song lyric playing in the background and start thinking about that, or I'll get a random idea for a completely different project. And suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing in the first place. It just happens all the time.
Do you often feel restless or like you have to move around when you’re supposed to sit still?

Yeah, definitely. Like, if I'm stuck on a long Zoom call for a lecture, or if I'm just supposed to be sitting quietly working on something, I start getting this weird, uncomfortable pressure in my body. It's like I just have to get up and pace around, or at least be doing something with my hands. Which reminds me, I actually bought this really cool fidget cube online last week. It has all these little buttons and switches on it, and it was supposed to be delivered yesterday, but the tracking app said there was a delay. I don't know why shipping is always so messed up lately. My roommate ordered a pair of shoes like three weeks ago and they still haven't shown up. She was so mad because she wanted to wear them to a party this weekend. But anyway, yeah, sitting still is super hard for me. I just feel like I need to be moving.
Have you often gotten into trouble for being impulsive, defiant, or acting out toward teachers, parents, or other authority figures?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm not mean to teachers or anything. I don't really act out. Actually, I had this one professor last semester for Intro to Psych, Dr. Harrison, and he was super strict. Like, if you were even two minutes late, he'd literally lock the door. Which is so unfair because the lecture hall is in the basement of the science building, and the elevators there are incredibly slow. 

One time, I got stuck in that elevator with this girl who had a pet iguana in her backpack. Like, a literal live iguana. She told me it was an emotional support animal, but I really don't think the school allows reptiles in the dorms. My RA told us during orientation we could only have fish. Which, honestly, fish are so boring. I had a betta fish in middle school named Barnaby and he just kind of floated there until he died. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, getting in trouble. Yeah, no, I'm usually pretty respectful to authority figures and stuff.
Did these attention and restlessness problems start before age 12?

Yeah, definitely way before I was 12. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing comments on my report cards about me rushing through my worksheets and completely losing track of directions. Which, speaking of worksheets, do you remember those timed multiplication things? The "Mad Minute" ones? I hated those so much. I always wanted to use my sparkly gel pens for them, but my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, made us use regular number two pencils. She was so obsessed with Ticonderoga pencils. Like, she literally had a giant cardboard cutout of a yellow pencil on her classroom door. I wonder if they still make those gel pens, actually... the ones that smelled like fruit? I had a strawberry one that I kept in this little fuzzy pencil case, and I took it everywhere until it leaked all over my backpack. 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the teacher comments! Yeah, they also complained that I was always talking over my classmates during group work. And at home, it was exactly the same. My parents used to have to sit right beside me at the kitchen table just so I'd do my homework, because otherwise I would completely wander off or start something else before finishing. Like, I'd go to the kitchen for a snack and end up trying to build a fort out of the living room sofa cushions. So, yeah, it's pretty much always been like this.
Have these restlessness or impulsive behaviors ever caused major problems at school, work, or in your relationships?

Um, yeah, I guess they have. Like, I do some freelance graphic design stuff on the side, just small contracts, but I've actually lost a couple of them because people felt like they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly. I just get so sidetracked. And I completely missed out on this huge portfolio competition last semester because I missed the deadline. Which was so annoying because I had this really awesome concept for a branding package for a fictional coffee shop. I even designed these little custom sleeves for the cups that looked like vintage library checkout cards. I love vintage library stuff. I actually bought this old wooden card catalog cabinet at a flea market last summer, thinking I'd use it to organize my art supplies. But it's so heavy, it's still just sitting in my parents' garage. My dad keeps asking when I'm going to move it, but honestly, I don't even know how I'd get it up the stairs to my apartment. 

But, um, anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, problems. Yeah, it's not just work stuff. It's kind of made some of my friends and people I collaborate with hesitant to work with me. Like, they always say they love my ideas, but when it comes to actually getting the project done, I think they get frustrated with me. So, yeah, it definitely causes some issues.
Before age 12, were you ever described as very hyperactive or 'always on the go'?

Um, before 12? I don't really think so. I mean, my parents never really called me hyperactive or anything like that. I was more just... I don't know, kind of in my own world? Like, I remember spending hours just sitting on my bedroom floor organizing my Polly Pockets. Did you ever have those? The original ones, not the big weird ones they make now. The tiny ones where the whole house folded up into a little plastic compact. I had this one that was shaped like a star and it had a tiny little ice skating rink inside. I used to make them skate around in circles for literally ever. My mom actually stepped on one of the tiny dolls once and it got stuck in her foot. She was so mad. She made me keep them all in this giant plastic tub after that, which completely ruined my whole display system. I had them color-coded by the outfits they were wearing, which was honestly a really good system. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, hyperactive. Yeah, no, I wasn't really bouncing off the walls or anything. Just, you know, easily distracted, like I said.
When you were a child, did teachers or your parents ever say you were unusually fidgety or couldn't stay seated?

Um, fidgety? Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I don't remember them specifically using the word "fidgety," but I definitely couldn't sit still for very long. It's actually still a thing for me now. Like, whenever I have to sit through meetings or those long portfolio reviews for my classes, I'm almost always bouncing my leg or clicking my pen. Or I'll twist my rings around. I have this one ring, actually, it's a silver spoon ring that I got at this really cute artisan market downtown. The girl who made it had this whole booth set up with all these vintage silver spoons and forks that she'd bent into jewelry. It was so cool. I bought a matching bracelet too, but it kept snagging on my sweaters, so I stopped wearing it. Sweaters are so annoying like that, especially the chunky knit ones. I love how they look, but they just catch on everything. 

Anyway... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the fidgeting. Yeah, I'll be twisting that ring or just shifting around in my chair a ton, and I don't even really notice I'm doing it until someone gives me a look or asks me to stop clicking my pen. So, yeah, I guess I've always been kind of restless like that, even if I wasn't running around the room.
